clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old male presented with fatigue, dizziness, acute renal failure, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and conjunctival jaundice. Initial labs showed hemolytic anemia (low Hb, reticulocytosis, elevated LDH, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, positive warm IgG Coombs test) and thrombocytopenia, consistent with Evan's syndrome. Further investigation for acute renal failure and other symptoms revealed a monoclonal gammopathy (IgG kappa M-protein in serum and urine) and significant plasma cell infiltration (78%) in the bone marrow. A whole-body CT scan showed multiple osteolytic lesions. Chemotherapy (bortezomib-thalidomide-dexamethasone) and corticosteroids were initiated, but the patient's condition deteriorated with worsening hematological and renal status, hemorrhagic symptoms, and ultimately death due to lactic acidosis.
